source.title: The Geometry of Meaning in Neural Manifolds

record.file_problem: The text is cut off at 400000 characters, before the thesis ends.
record.tranche_reason: The thesis reports its own experiments measuring representational alignment and interchangeability using correspondence-based projections, transformations, retrieval, and stitching. These are conceptual tests of convergence and alignment, not a scale sweep using the original sources’ methods.
record.gate_note: The thesis includes results from multiple methods and applications. Rows below retain results that directly measure cross-model alignment or whether representations can be transformed and reused, and results showing metric dependence or incomplete transfer. Background claims and results cited from other work are not recorded as rows. ASIF’s cross-modal classification and its dataset-size results do not measure whether paired image and caption representations become more aligned as both models improve.
record.test_reason: The thesis directly measures cross-seed similarity, cross-model retrieval, and representation interchangeability, and tests dependence on projection and data. Its Cora experiments also bear on the capability component of V1, although they do not establish convergence with model size.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase agrees with the supplied abstract and framework discussion: semantic correspondence exposes exploitable shared geometry and enables model reuse, with empirical limits from correspondence quality and geometric assumptions. The actual concluding chapter is absent, so its wording cannot be verified.
record.recipe_differences: The thesis tests a collection of correspondence-based methods, including relative representations, orthogonal or affine translation, and latent functional maps; it does not reproduce the original sources’ methods as a scale-and-capability sweep.
record.method_sensitivity: The thesis reports dependence on projection metric, dataset, architecture, and anchor quantity. For the product-of-invariances experiments, the best single metric varies by model and dataset; the product also loses to a single metric in one reported image condition.

fits_no_version.finding: ResiDual and HeadPursuit identify specialized components and improve or steer individual models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Semantic information can be concentrated in specialized components within a model.

fits_no_version.finding: Human fMRI representations become more comparable across subjects after task-informed encoding and relative projection.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Correspondence can expose shared structure across human neural recordings.

record.peer_reviewed: Doctoral thesis; chapter publications list venues including ICLR, NeurIPS, and TMLR.
record.problems: The supplied text is truncated. Several relevant comparisons are presented only in figures, and some results measure downstream stitching performance rather than representation similarity directly. The thesis compiles methods with different settings and does not isolate the causal effects of model scale, capability, shared data, or shared objectives.
record.rows_left_out: The thesis reports many additional per-dataset, per-model, per-metric, and per-anchor-count results, especially in Tables 5.2-5.5, 10.2, 11.1-11.3, and 12.4. They are not all listed because the retained rows capture the principal cross-model alignment findings, metric dependence, and incomplete transfer within the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: Increasing model size, systematic scaling across independently varied architectures, objectives and training data, and convergence toward a universal limit. The Cora result concerns capability relative to a fixed reference.
Whether paired vision-language representation alignment increases as both encoders improve. Cross-modal classification performance and correspondence-dataset scaling do not establish this.
The fraction of learned features or subspaces shared across seeds is not quantified by the retained rows.

General interchangeability for arbitrary model pairs, and low-loss cross-model mapping with neither paired examples nor shared labels. Label-based anchor-free stitching still uses semantic supervision.
Recurrence of matched interpretable features or circuits across independently trained models. Within-model head specialization does not establish recurrence.
Systematic neighbor-count sensitivity and universal disappearance of convergence out of distribution.
Plateauing with scale and causal attribution to shared training data or objectives rather than a common model of reality.

missing.what: Capability–alignment association across approximately 2,000 Cora models, plus within-training mean Pearson correlation 0.955 after excluding models with best validation accuracy below 0.5.

Cross-seed reconstruction stitching with matched non-stitch controls. Relative AE average reconstruction MSE rises from 2.78 to 8.16, and relative VAE from 5.22 to 14.97, in units of 10^-3; substantial gains over absolute stitching coexist with reconstruction loss.
Cross-architecture representational similarity changes with the infused invariance and dataset; no projection consistently dominates.

Cross-seed and cross-variation CarRacing stitching: matching green components from different seeds score 781 ± 108 with R3L versus 175 ± 304 with absolute representations; transfer is weaker for camera-distance and slow-task conditions.

Projection-dependent alignment of ensemble latent representations: cosine works best for VGG-16, Euclidean for PreResNet-110, and Euclidean projection can reduce VGG-16 alignment over early curve positions. Distinguish independently trained endpoints from fitted intermediate models.

record.verdict_notes: The thesis is not one of the listed original sources. Conclusions concern the supplied excerpt, which ends during Section 14.3.2. Results explicitly declared omitted in rows_left_out are not repeated as missing. V6 and the incomplete-alignment component of V7 receive supports when their predicted limitations occur; those observations do not warrant limits_scope labels for the challenge versions themselves.

versions.untested_parts: The thesis discusses differences in architecture, data, and training objectives, but does not test whether alignment rises as model size and capability increase.
ASIF uses image-text pairs, but the reported results do not test whether vision-language alignment increases as both models improve.
The thesis does not establish that the same individual features recur across seeds; the reported cross-seed evidence concerns geometric similarity and stitching.
The experiments do not test every mapping type named in the claim, in particular mapping without paired data across all settings.
The thesis analyzes component specialization, but does not test whether the same interpretable features or circuits recur across different models.
The reported metric-dependence experiments vary projection functions and datasets; they do not systematically test neighbour-count settings or out-of-distribution inputs across all alignment methods.
The thesis reports incomplete transfer and conditions affecting alignment, but does not isolate the causal contribution of shared training data or objectives from other causes.

rows.subject: CViT-B/32 encoder and ViT-B/16 decoder
rows.operation_detail: Compared zero-shot stitching using single relative projections with the product of four projections.

conditions.value: Cosine, Euclidean, L1, L∞, or product with aggregation by sum

rows.note: Metric choice changes the result; the product is higher than the single projections in this condition.
rows.check: The metric differences directly support V6. For V4, the row lacks the corresponding end-to-end accuracy needed to determine whether stitching incurs little loss; split the two assessments.

rows.subject: RViT-B/16 encoder and ViT-B/16 decoder
rows.operation_detail: Compared zero-shot stitching using single relative projections with the product of four projections.

conditions.value: L1 or product with aggregation by sum

rows.note: The text identifies this as the exception among eight image cells where the product loses to the best single projection.
rows.check: Remove V7: product versus single-projection accuracy does not establish incomplete geometric convergence or its causes. V6 is observed across the full metric comparison, including L∞ at 0.60 ± 0.03. The 0.03 product-versus-L1 difference alone is not an established significant deterioration. V4's little-loss component needs an end-to-end baseline.

rows.subject: AEs and VAEs trained from scratch
rows.operation_detail: Compared cross-seed latent-space similarity after different relative projections.

conditions.value: Cosine, Euclidean, L1; L∞ not displayed

rows.value: Figure only; text states that different projection types yield the highest similarity for VAE versus LinVAE and that no single projection consistently outperforms the others.
rows.note: Results vary by architecture and dataset; the text explicitly challenges reliance on a single invariance.
rows.check: The supplied figure extraction does not provide readable correlation magnitudes sufficient to grade V3. The accompanying text explicitly establishes V6: the best projection changes with architecture and dataset. Split this into a V3 magnitude assessment and an observed V6 result.

rows.subject: Pretrained vision and language encoders with SVM decoders
rows.operation_detail: Compared zero-shot stitching by direct translation with the unstitched decoder and untransformed absolute representations.
rows.note: Translation supports interchangeability, but does not recover the no-stitch score in this condition.
rows.check: The affine value is correct, but it is not the best method: ortho reaches 0.71 ± 0.09 versus no-stitch 0.76 ± 0.09. Restrict the subject to vision encoders for this dataset. Remove V7: downstream accuracy loss does not independently quantify incomplete representational convergence.

rows.subject: Pretrained vision and language encoders with SVM decoders
rows.operation_detail: Compared zero-shot stitching by direct translation with the unstitched decoder and untransformed absolute representations.

conditions.value: Best reported method: affine or ortho, both 0.66

rows.note: The thesis identifies DBpedia as the largest reported drop from no-stitch performance.
rows.check: Restrict the subject to language encoders. Remove V7: the task-performance gap establishes a limitation of interchangeability, without isolating geometric convergence or its causes. Reported variability is across heterogeneous pairs and runs, not a significance test.

rows.subject: FastText and Word2Vec
rows.operation_detail: Measured retrieval after learning a latent functional map and fitting an orthogonal transformation from its inferred correspondences.

conditions.value: 18K held-out words from a 20K shared vocabulary

rows.baseline: Competing methods are reported as lower at 300 anchors; exact values not stated in the text.
rows.note: The text also reports MRR over 0.8 with just 5 anchors.
rows.check: Retain the held-out retrieval result. Clarify that graphs use 2K corresponding vocabulary samples, with 300 anchors in the reported condition; the experiment does not demonstrate alignment without paired data.

relationships.condition: Cora node classifiers compared with a well-performing reference
